analysis:
Two files changed. The first is .github/workflows/ci.yml (patch near line 380, in the test-provider-sdk job): it adds CI steps that run nested suites for native historical retention, demanded checkpoint partition and continuation, and one MiMo native retention test. The new steps use the existing run-nested-suite.sh wrapper and the existing fixture-preparation script with --asymmetric, writing under $RUNNER_TEMP. They add no secrets, no new permissions, no new third-party actions, and no change to untrusted-input handling. They only add test coverage, which is neutral to positive.

The second is CHANGELOG.md, which is documentation only. It describes behavior changes in the prefix-cache area: retention of a demanded shared-prefix checkpoint, and giving authenticated repeated checkpoints access to the reserved SSD write share on first local appearance. It also describes bounded COMPLETE-donation hashing and first-content token-budget reconciliation. The source for these behaviors is not in this batch, so I could not review the code.

Relevance to T-041 (cross-tenant prefix cache and the TTFT oracle, SEC-035): the changelog says demanded checkpoints are retained more readily and that repeated checkpoints get SSD write priority. This could slightly widen cache-hit observability and at-rest activity. The entry says addresses stay authenticated and that account/alias policy and the endpoint rules are preserved. No code in this batch contradicts the T-041 account-scoped salt, HMAC lookup tag, TTL or disk-budget mitigations.

The next review pass should check the actual Swift changes in the KVCacheSSD and CBv2 prefix-cache sources once supplied. In particular: (1) SSDPrefixCache.donate gating for the repeated-checkpoint write share; (2) that on-disk names and metadata remain HMAC-only; (3) that cacheSalt scoping is preserved for demanded checkpoints; (4) the TTL and disk reserve. Also check the first-content token-budget reconciliation on the coordinator side for any billing or deadline-bypass effect. No findings from these two units.
